lab_title: The Molecular Mechanics of DNA Structure and Semiconservative Replication
top_level_objectives: Identify the components and geometry of the DNA double helix.
Apply base-pairing rules to construct a complementary DNA strand.
Differentiate between the 5' and 3' ends and understand the significance of antiparallel orientation.
Explain the functional roles of Helicase, DNA Polymerase, and Ligase in replication.
Distinguish between leading and lagging strand synthesis mechanisms.
Demonstrate why the process is defined as semiconservative.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the 3D structure of the DNA double helix.
key_visuals: Floating 3D model of a DNA segment showing the double helix, sugar-phosphate backbones, and interior base pairs.
student_actions: Rotate and zoom in on the helix to observe the intertwined strands.
Select specific components (sugar, phosphate, nitrogenous base) to highlight their chemical identity.

key_visuals: Close-up view of the interior of the helix, highlighting A-T and G-C pairings.
student_actions: Attempt to pair free-floating nucleotides to their corresponding partner on an exposed template strand.
Observe the hydrogen bond indicators (2 bonds for A-T, 3 for G-C) that glow upon correct pairing.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the antiparallel orientation of DNA strands.
key_visuals: DNA helix with directional arrows along the sugar-phosphate backbones; 5' and 3' labels.
student_actions: Toggle the 5' to 3' polarity markers to see the directional contrast between the two strands.
Rotate the molecule to verify that the strands run in opposite directions.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the initiation of DNA replication.
key_visuals: Replication fork with Helicase enzyme appearing at a bubble and Single-Strand Binding Proteins (SSBs) attaching to the opened strands.
student_actions: Place the Helicase enzyme onto the double helix to trigger unwinding.
Observe the stabilization of the template strands by SSBs to prevent re-annealing.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the continuous synthesis of the leading strand.
key_visuals: DNA Polymerase moving toward the replication fork, extending a new strand in the 5' to 3' direction.
student_actions: Guide the DNA Polymerase enzyme along the template to witness the continuous addition of complementary nucleotides.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the discontinuous synthesis of the lagging strand.
key_visuals: DNA Polymerase moving away from the fork; multiple fragments (Okazaki fragments) appearing; DNA Ligase joining them.
student_actions: Observe the backward movement of the polymerase on the lagging strand template.
Tap the DNA Ligase enzyme to seal the nicks between completed Okazaki fragments.

scenes.brief_purpose: Confirm the semiconservative nature of replication.
key_visuals: Two finished DNA double helices, with parental strands colored blue and new strands colored gold.
student_actions: Compare the final two DNA molecules to confirm each contains one original template and one new strand.
Rotate the final models to inspect the structural integrity of the newly synthesized helices.
